set.body:
The README is the document meant to win a trial, and roughly a third of its code cannot be executed by the reader.

11 R code blocks. Only 7 lines of output are shown anywhere, and all 7 come from the single contrast table. rdm, rsa, geometry_spectrum and connectivity are all shown WITH NO OUTPUT AT ALL - so the reader is shown the call and never the result, for four of the package five headline verbs.

Worse, the crossnobis block at README:322-333 references X, C, L, response_runs and condition_contrast, and NONE of the five is defined anywhere in the README. It sits in a plain r fence visually identical to the runnable block at the top, so nothing signals to a reader that copying it will fail. The prior reviewer of this package independently executed all 11 blocks and found the same thing: 7 run clean, 3 fail on undefined objects (lm_extractor, lm_relation_fit, plan_crossnobis).

Illustrative pseudo-code is a legitimate style. Illustrative pseudo-code that is typographically indistinguishable from runnable code is not, because the reader cannot tell which is which until it errors.

Note the interaction with the vignettes, which makes this worse than it looks in isolation: introduction.Rmd has lm_extractor in exactly one chunk and it is eval=FALSE at :347, lm_relation_fit appears in prose only, and crossnobis appears ZERO times in either vignette. So the raw-fMRI entry path - which the hands-on trial confirmed is where a real user starts - has NO executable documentation anywhere outside the test suite and a single Rd example.

FIX, cheapest first:
  1. mark the illustrative blocks as such, visually and unambiguously
  2. show output for rdm, rsa, geometry_spectrum and connectivity - the values already exist,
     they are simply not printed
  3. once a generator exists (bd-01KZY8KX8R32RR4T6741XTJXKT), the crossnobis block becomes
     runnable rather than illustrative, which closes this and the vignette gap together
set.title: README code blocks: 4 of 11 do not run, and the crossnobis block references five objects defined nowhere
